verdict.whatTheRulingMeans: The blocking defect this successor exists to repair is CLOSED, and I proved it end to end rather than reading the claim. The separation between MEASUREMENT and PIN is complete for the channel that mattered: I could not find any path by which content in an unpinned document reaches exec. The instrument's remaining weaknesses are all inside the surface it already declares as bounded, plus one new limit I found that narrows a sentence it publishes about itself. None of them is reachable by an adversary who can only write documents, which is the adversary the repair was written against.
verdict.whatTheRulingDoesNotMean: It does not mean the AST self-audit is complete -- IR-NPAV3-01 measures four execution edges it does not notice. It does not mean the finding sets are correct in general; I graded the classes the brief named and re-derived the figures I relied on, and I did not audit NPA-1's precision predicates or NPA-6's PLAN-ID-V1 semantics.

claim1_theRepairsShape.question: Is the separation between MEASUREMENT and PIN complete, or is there a path to execution that bypasses the gate?
claim1_theRepairsShape.answer: COMPLETE for every path I could construct. I found no route from document content to exec.

theAttackReproducedOnBothVersions.method: A full byte-copy of docs/coop per variant. The hostile oracle replaces artifacts/check-d9-v1.14.py with a payload that WRITES A MARKER FILE and then RAISES. ONE digest string -- the payload's own sha256 f3e446bc321e960adfd0148f7b2d00b75f153adfe0ee21fc726665e5bb97125f -- was inserted into IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md immediately before the first occurrence of the filename. That is the whole attack: 67 bytes added to an unpinned document, plus attacker-chosen module bytes. The blueprint went 206084 -> 206151 bytes.

v2_result.conclusion: THE PAYLOAD EXECUTED. Arbitrary code ran, on a single string inserted into a document v2 does not pin. Reproduced independently; this is not read from the brief.
v2_result.additionalObservationAboutV2: v2's own skip text reads '...so this is not drift; the module did not run'. The module DID run -- it wrote the marker before raising. v2 misreports its own execution in the one line a reader would use to decide whether anything ran. v2 is not my subject and I raise this only because it sharpens what the successor had to repair.

v3_result.message: live f3e446bc... != pinned 513d69dd.... This file EXECUTES that module, so freeze section 7.3 requires the hash to hold before the bytes run, and they were NOT run.
v3_result.conclusion: The payload never reached exec, NPA-5 was skipped BY NAME, and the other five classes kept measuring.

theAttackReproducedOnBothVersions.theAuthorsEvidenceDesignGraded: The hostile oracle RAISES if executed. So the two refusal tokens are mutually exclusive evidence: NPA-PIN-EXEC-FAILED would prove the bytes reached exec, and NPA-PIN-DRIFT proves they did not. Seeing PIN-DRIFT is therefore a POSITIVE proof of non-execution, not merely an absence of the marker. This is the right way to build the evidence and I confirmed it independently with the marker file as a second, redundant channel: exit code and filesystem agree. The subject's own suite encodes the same design as an assertion, printing '[never NPA-PIN-EXEC-FAILED: True]' on the two oracle cases.

theSeparationAudited.measurementSurvives: digests_recorded_near() still scrapes the +/-400-character window and publishes the result as oracleDigestsRecordedInDocs. On live bytes it finds three 64-hex strings near the oracle's name and the pinned one is among them, so NPA-5-ORACLE-PIN-UNRECORDED does not fire.
theSeparationAudited.measurementAuthorisesNothing: Verified structurally and by execution. The recorded set is compared to EXECUTED_PINS[mod_rel]['sha256'] and the comparison's only consequence is a FINDING. load_pinned_module() never reads it: the expected digest comes from the table literal. Grep confirms DIGEST_WINDOW and the recorded set are referenced only inside check_npa_5, never inside the gate.
theSeparationAudited.orderOfOperations: read -> hash -> compare -> exec, in that order, at lines 781-804, with the raise between the compare and the exec. Freeze section 7.3 satisfied.
theSeparationAudited.cacheDoesNotWeakenTheGate: _PINNED_MODULES is keyed on the ACTUAL digest, not the path, and the cache hit is guarded by `actual == expected` as well. A selftest overlay supplying different bytes for a pinned path therefore cannot be served a module built from other bytes. I read this specifically because a path-keyed cache is the obvious way this repair would have been silently undone, and it is not what is there.
theSeparationAudited.auditRunsBeforeAnythingExecutes: run_check() calls audit_execution_surface() at line 1718 and raises before the first read of the packet. Nothing is executed if the audit disagrees.
otherRoutesIConsideredAndRejected: resolve_dotted() walks a getattr chain built from attacker-editable text after '::' in referenceDerivation, so an attacker can reach arbitrary attributes of the ALREADY-EXECUTED pinned module (e.g. __builtins__.exec). Not an execution edge: the resolved object is passed to inspect.signature and compared to blueprint text as a string. It is never called.
Symlinking a pinned path elsewhere: the digest is taken of the bytes actually read, so the pin still binds.
Path traversal in rel: the gate matches EXECUTED_PINS keys by exact string, so a traversal string is simply absent from the table and refused.
Naming check-package-coherence.py as the oracle: it IS pinned, so it would load, but it is already loaded and no new code executes.

claim1_theRepairsShape.grade: The repair's shape is right and the shape is the point. v2 used a value the adversary can write as the gate; v3 uses it as a claim about the documents and gates on a table the adversary cannot reach without editing the reviewed bytes. Freeze section 7.2.2's axis applied correctly one level up, and the axis is the correct one.

claim2_theSelfAudit.question: Try to add an execution edge it does not notice.
claim2_theSelfAudit.answer: I added four, and it noticed none of them. All four are plainly static, fully resolvable AST nodes. See IR-NPAV3-01.
whatTheAuditDoesWell: It is DERIVED from the running source rather than typed, so a constant that merely SPELLS exec(compile( is not a Call node and drops out for free.

It enforces BOTH directions: nothing outside the gate, and the gate must still contain its own compile and exec. I tested the second limb myself by replacing the gate's exec(compile(...)) with `pass`; the run refused at exit 2 with NPA-EXEC-AUDIT-DISAGREES naming both missing sites. That limb is unexercised by the suite and it works.
It refuses at exit 2 rather than reporting -- freeze section 7.2.2's rider satisfied, a measurement that CAN fail the build.
It prints the four sites with primitive, scope and line on every normal run, so the published account is regenerated from the surface each time.

importlib's loader protocol is covered in full (module_from_spec, spec_from_loader, spec_from_file_location, exec_module, create_module, import_module, load_module, reload, run_path, run_module, exec_dynamic), which is genuinely the route a successor author is most likely to take after the builtins.
claim2_theSelfAudit.whatItDoesNotNotice: See IR-NPAV3-01 for the measurement. The predicate is a hand-enumerated vocabulary, and everything outside that vocabulary is invisible even when it is written in plain sight.

claim4_noRegression.L4sFigureIsDerivedNotTyped: L-4 publishes '6 of its 11 REJECT-carrying blocks disclose on the same LINE as its name'. The banner's rejectDisclosureSameLine recomputes exactly that on every run and prints rust-provider-protocol.v2@IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE 6; my own independent count of disclosing occurrences in that document was 11. Both halves agree. This is a limit whose severity figure cannot go stale, which is the right way to publish one.

designStrengths: Scoring is FINDING-SET DELTA against the base run, on (id, detail) fingerprints -- a positive case passes only by ADDING a finding the base lacked, and a negative passes only if the delta is empty in BOTH directions. This is the right unit and it makes 'the base was already red' unable to launder a pass.

NB-4's no-op detection is applied to EVERY case in EVERY suite, not just negatives, and a no-op FAILS the build. The asymmetry is correctly reasoned in the docstring: positives are fail-safe under a no-op, negatives are not.
The gates include both directions of the pin table -- nothing executes unpinned (structural) AND no pin is dead weight (measured against the base run's modulesExecutedThisRun).
NB-8's peer heuristic is run over the subject's own source and FAILS if it attributes an edge, so the self-exclusion at line 1482 is asserted rather than incidental.

Fixtures are DERIVED, not named: the NPA-1 fixture is the first STATUS-graded row the class itself finds in v1-slice.md and the NPA-2 fabricated row comes from the packet's own decided ids, so no live corpus identifier is written into any predicate. This is the corpus's own lesson -- an instrument that hard-codes an example of what it hunts becomes an instance of it -- applied correctly.

nonBlockingFindings.severity: non-blocking, and the sharpest thing in this review
nonBlockingFindings.title: The execution-surface audit's vocabulary is HAND-ENUMERATED, so four plainly-static execution edges outside the gate are invisible while the banner reports the audit as complete
nonBlockingFindings.class: freeze section 7.2.2's ENUMERATION failure mode -- hand-listed rather than derived -- committed inside the audit that the file built to close the prose-cannot-notice-a-second-edge problem

measurement.method: Four doctored byte-copies of the subject, one execution edge each, inserted at module scope immediately after the import block. Each run as a real process with -I -B against a full copy of the tree.

results.banner: AST AUDIT of these bytes: 4 execution primitive(s), all inside load_pinned_module()

theInversionThatMakesItCrisp.harmlessEdgeCAUGHT: __import__('json') -- imports an already-loaded stdlib module and executes nothing new -- REFUSED at exit 2 with NPA-EXEC-AUDIT-DISAGREES.
theInversionThatMakesItCrisp.harmfulEdgeMISSED: import evilmod2 -- executes an attacker-supplied file's module-level code -- exit 0, green, marker written.
theInversionThatMakesItCrisp.why: EXEC_CALL_NAMES contains __import__, so the DYNAMIC form of an import is an audited edge. EXEC_IMPORT_NAMES contains only runpy and subprocess, so the STATIC form is audited only for two module names. The audit is stricter about the safe spelling than about the dangerous one.

whatThisFalsifies: Line 1484-1490, the stated justification for excluding the subject from its own NPA-4 census: 'What makes it harmless is a PROPERTY, not an intention: this file imports no `subprocess` and invokes no external binary, and its own execution-surface audit refuses the run if that ever stops being true.' MEASURED FALSE in its second half. With os.system or os.posix_spawn at module scope the file DOES invoke an external binary and the audit does NOT refuse. The exclusion is safe today because of what the bytes happen to be, which is an INTENTION, not the property the comment claims.
Docstring line 211-212: 'the AST audit proves the gate is the only site.' It proves the gate is the only site for four enumerated primitive families.
L-15's clause 'it proves the declared gate is the only site in THIS file'. Same correction.
nonBlockingFindings.whyItIsNotL6L13L14OrL15: L-14 is about a primitive 'reached through a name it cannot resolve' -- getattr(__builtins__, 'e'+'xec'), a dict lookup. All four of my edges are fully resolvable, plainly named AST nodes that the parser sees perfectly; the predicate simply does not ask about them. L-13 is transitive execution by a module the subject executes; these are edges in the subject's OWN static surface, which is precisely what L-13 says the audit DOES bind. L-6 is about NPA-4's census over other checkers. None of the fifteen covers this.
nonBlockingFindings.theSharpestPart: The file ALREADY CARRIES the wider predicate. SUBPROCESS_CALLS, OS_SHELL_CALLS and OS_PROGRAM_CALLS (with per-API program-name indices, added deliberately as NB-2) are applied to 116 other checkers by NPA-4 and are not applied to the subject's own self-audit. The instrument hunts os.system, os.execvp, os.spawnlp and posix_spawn across the corpus and cannot see the same call in itself.
whyItIsNOTBLOCKING: The live bytes are clean. Verified by AST: the complete import set is __future__, typing, ast, hashlib, importlib.util, inspect, json, pathlib, re, sys. No os, subprocess, runpy, ctypes, marshal, types, pickle, shutil or socket, and no call whose base is any of them. There is nothing to exploit in the reviewed bytes.

Every escape requires editing the subject's own source. Freeze section 7.2 covers that with the digest, and L-15 names the right remedy: a reviewer records the digest and the corpus compares it. That protection is real and this review records the digest.

The load-bearing guard against the adversary the repair was written for -- one who can write documents -- is load_pinned_module's refusal of any path absent from EXECUTED_PINS, and that guard is complete. I could not get past it.
nonBlockingFindings.whatItCosts: The audit's value is as a guard for the NEXT author. The docstring's argument for building it is exact: 'v2's claim of exactly one was prose, and prose cannot notice a second edge being added.' A v4 author who adds `import somehelper`, or reaches for os.system rather than subprocess, gets a green audit and a banner asserting the surface is unchanged. The audit is a NECESSARY condition that reads as a sufficient one, and its own banner line is what makes it read that way.
nonBlockingFindings.suggestedRepairForASUCCESSOR_notAnEditTo: Three cheap moves, in order of value. (1) Treat EVERY ast.Import / ast.ImportFrom of a non-stdlib-allowlisted module as an edge, rather than flagging two names -- derive the allowlist from sys.stdlib_module_names and require any addition to be declared. (2) Reuse the file's OWN OS_SHELL_CALLS / OS_PROGRAM_CALLS / SUBPROCESS_CALLS tables inside audit_execution_surface, so the self-audit is at least as wide as the census it runs over 116 peers. (3) Reword the banner from 'all inside load_pinned_module()' to name the vocabulary it searched, so a reader can see the predicate's edge. None of this can be done to these bytes; freeze section 7.2 requires a successor.

nonBlockingFindings.title: An emptied IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md produces three NPA-1 findings that name v1-slice.md -- a correct document -- and the finding text never says the register was empty

nonBlockingFindings.theShape: The CAUSE is that the freeze is empty. The ACCUSATION names v1-slice.md as presenting decided rows as unresolved. Freeze section 7.8.1's class: an input's damage presenting as a substantive finding partly about a different artifact.
whatMitigatesIt_statedFairly: The finding STATEMENT also names freeze section 5.1 ('and freeze section 5.1 does not record the disagreement'), so a reader following it reaches the empty document and discovers the cause. This is materially weaker misdirection than the predecessor's case, where the accusation was purely against section 5.1 while the damaged input was v1-slice.md.
The banner publishes disagreementsRecorded 0 (against 3 on the live tree), subjectsGraded 0, rejectSubjectsNamedByBothDocs [] and the freeze's own digest, so the state is legible to a careful reader.

The design choice is defensible and is the safer of the two available. Refusing when section 5.1 is absent would let anyone buy silence by deleting the register heading -- which is exactly what the suite's first positive case exists to prevent. Making it a finding is right.

Nothing about the finding set changes; the reader is told which document to open first. Recorded as unnamed in all fifteen limits.
nonBlockingFindings.boundOnThisFinding: The findings are LITERALLY TRUE under the instrument's own definition of agreement, and the instrument holds no opinion about acceptability. I am grading the readability of a true finding, not its correctness.

nonBlockingFindings.title: A truncated or emptied copy of the subject exits 0 with NO OUTPUT AT ALL, which the instrument's own exit table reads as 'ran completely and found nothing'
nonBlockingFindings.measurement: Subject replaced with zero bytes: exit 0, stdout 0 bytes, stderr 0 bytes. Subject truncated to half its length (70642 bytes): exit 0, stdout 0 bytes, stderr 0 bytes. Both in a full tree copy, run as real processes.
nonBlockingFindings.why: This is a property of running a Python file rather than a logic defect -- an empty program exits 0. But the subject publishes an exit-code contract in which 0 means 'the check RAN COMPLETELY and found nothing', and this is the one state that contract cannot cover from inside itself.
nonBlockingFindings.whatAlreadyCoversIt: Freeze section 7.2's digest recording, which this review performs, and L-15, which names the right boundary ('it cannot prove that this file is the file anyone reviewed'). A truncated file has a different digest and is caught by the corpus discipline, not by the instrument.
nonBlockingFindings.whatIsUnnamed: L-15 is framed around SUBSTITUTION -- an edit that adds a site and updates the pins and the gate together. TRUNCATION TO SILENCE is a different shape and the more likely accident (a partial checkout, a failed write, a truncated copy). It is also the shape a CI rule reading only exit codes misreads most cleanly: exit 0 with an empty banner is the one output no rule of the form 'exit 0 means green' can distinguish from a pass.
nonBlockingFindings.cheapMitigationForASUCCESSOR: Nothing inside the file can fix it. A caller-side rule can: require the banner's first line on stdout, not merely exit 0. Worth one sentence in the exit-code block.

nonBlockingFindings.title: NPA-3's disclosure test matches the artifact STEM, so occurrences of longer artifact names sharing that stem count toward disclosure

All four graded subjects have longer siblings sharing their stem -- threat-model.v3 has three (review-reviewer1, review-reviewer2, storage-namespace.review-independent), rust-provider-protocol.v2 has three, c2-plan-stage-schema.v3 has two, retention-tiers.v25 has one. nonBlockingFindings.doesItCarryTheLoadToday: NO. I measured all 8 (subject x document) cells: in every one, disclosure rests on BARE-STEM occurrences -- 5/5, 2/2, 2/2, 3/3, 11/11, 5/5, 10/10, 7/7. There is no cell whose disclosure depends only on a longer-name occurrence.
nonBlockingFindings.grade: Latent, adjacent to L-4's attribution family rather than separate from it, and not worth a limit of its own on today's bytes. Recorded so a successor author knows the stem match is doing more work than it appears to.
